paragraphs.text: And when he entered again into Capernaum after some days, it was noised that he was in the house.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἰσελθὼν πάλιν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ διʼ ἡμερῶν ἠκούσθη ὅτι ἐν οἴκῳ ἐστίν·
paragraphs.translit: Kai eiselthōn palin eis Kapharnaoum diʼ hēmerōn ēkousthē hoti en oikō estin·

paragraphs.text: And many were gathered together, so that there was no longer room [for them], no, not even about the door: and he spake the word unto them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ συνήχθησαν πολλοὶ ὥστε μηκέτι χωρεῖν μηδὲ τὰ πρὸς τὴν θύραν, καὶ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον.
paragraphs.translit: kai synēchthēsan polloi hōste mēketi chōrein mēde ta pros tēn thyran, kai elalei autois ton logon.

paragraphs.text: And they come, bringing unto him a man sick of the palsy, borne of four.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔρχονται φέροντες πρὸς αὐτὸν παραλυτικὸν αἰρόμενον ὑπὸ τεσσάρων.
paragraphs.translit: kai erchontai pherontes pros auton paralytikon airomenon hypo tessarōn.

paragraphs.text: And when they could not come nigh unto him for the crowd, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed whereon the sick of the palsy lay.
paragraphs.original: καὶ μὴ δυνάμενοι προσενέγκαι αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀπεστέγασαν τὴν στέγην ὅπου ἦν, καὶ ἐξορύξαντες χαλῶσι τὸν κράβαττον ὅπου ὁ παραλυτικὸς κατέκειτο.
paragraphs.translit: kai mē dynamenoi prosenenkai autō dia ton ochlon apestegasan tēn stegēn hopou ēn, kai exoryxantes chalōsi ton krabatton hopou ho paralytikos katekeito.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus seeing their faith saith unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins are forgiven.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Τέκνον, ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.
paragraphs.translit: kai idōn ho Iēsous tēn pistin autōn legei tō paralytikō· Teknon, aphientai sou hai hamartiai.

paragraphs.text: But there were certain of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,
paragraphs.original: ἦσαν δέ τινες τῶν γραμματέων ἐκεῖ καθήμενοι καὶ διαλογιζόμενοι ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν·
paragraphs.translit: ēsan de tines tōn grammateōn ekei kathēmenoi kai dialogizomenoi en tais kardiais autōn·

paragraphs.text: Why doth this man thus speak? he blasphemeth: who can forgive sins but one, [even] God?
paragraphs.original: Τί οὗτος οὕτως λαλεῖ; βλασφημεῖ· τίς δύναται ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας εἰ μὴ εἷς ὁ θεός;
paragraphs.translit: Ti houtos houtōs lalei; blasphēmei· tis dynatai aphienai hamartias ei mē heis ho theos;

paragraphs.text: And straightway Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, saith unto them, Why reason ye these things in your hearts?
paragraphs.original: καὶ εὐθὺς ἐπιγνοὺς ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ ὅτι οὕτως διαλογίζονται ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί ταῦτα διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: kai euthys epignous ho Iēsous tō pneumati autou hoti houtōs dialogizontai en heautois legei autois· Ti tauta dialogizesthe en tais kardiais hymōn;

paragraphs.text: Which is easier, to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins are forgiven; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?
paragraphs.original: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν τῷ παραλυτικῷ· Ἀφίενταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι, ἢ εἰπεῖν· Ἔγειρε καὶ ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει;
paragraphs.translit: ti estin eukopōteron, eipein tō paralytikō· Aphientai sou hai hamartiai, ē eipein· Egeire kai aron ton krabatton sou kai peripatei;

paragraphs.text: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath authority on earth to forgive sins (he saith to the sick of the palsy),
paragraphs.original: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας— λέγει τῷ παραλυτικῷ·
paragraphs.translit: hina de eidēte hoti exousian echei ho hyios tou anthrōpou epi tēs gēs aphienai hamartias— legei tō paralytikō·

paragraphs.text: I say unto thee, Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thy house.
paragraphs.original: Σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειρε ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ ὕπαγε εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.
paragraphs.translit: Soi legō, egeire aron ton krabatton sou kai hypage eis ton oikon sou.

paragraphs.text: And he arose, and straightway took up the bed, and went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἠγέρθη καὶ εὐθὺς ἄρας τὸν κράβαττον ἐξῆλθεν ἔμπροσθεν πάντων, ὥστε ἐξίστασθαι πάντας καὶ δοξάζειν τὸν θεὸν λέγοντας ὅτι Οὕτως οὐδέποτε εἴδομεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēgerthē kai euthys aras ton krabatton exēlthen emprosthen pantōn, hōste existasthai pantas kai doxazein ton theon legontas hoti Houtōs oudepote eidomen.

paragraphs.text: And he went forth again by the sea side; and all the multitude resorted unto him, and he taught them.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν πάλιν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρχετο πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai exēlthen palin para tēn thalassan· kai pas ho ochlos ērcheto pros auton, kai edidasken autous.

paragraphs.text: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the [son] of Alphaeus sitting at the place of toll, and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ παράγων εἶδεν Λευὶν τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι. καὶ ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai paragōn eiden Leuin ton tou Halphaiou kathēmenon epi to telōnion, kai legei autō· Akolouthei moi. kai anastas ēkolouthēsen autō.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, that he was sitting at meat in his house, and many publicans and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples: for there were many, and they followed him.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ γίνεται κατακεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ, καὶ πολλοὶ τελῶναι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ συνανέκειντο τῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ, ἦσαν γὰρ πολλοὶ καὶ ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ginetai katakeisthai auton en tē oikia autou, kai polloi telōnai kai hamartōloi synanekeinto tō Iēsou kai tois mathētais autou, ēsan gar polloi kai ēkolouthoun autō.

paragraphs.text: And the scribes of the Pharisees, when they saw that he was eating with the sinners and publicans, said unto his disciples, [How is it] that he eateth and drinketh with publicans and sinners?
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τῶν Φαρισαίων ἰδόντες ὅτι ἐσθίει μετὰ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν καὶ τελωνῶν ἔλεγον τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ· Ὅτι μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίει;
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi grammateis tōn Pharisaiōn idontes hoti esthiei meta tōn hamartōlōn kai telōnōn elegon tois mathētais autou· Hoti meta tōn telōnōn kai hamartōlōn esthiei;

paragraphs.text: And when Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of a physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀκούσας ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ἰσχύοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλʼ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες· οὐκ ἦλθον καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς.
paragraphs.translit: kai akousas ho Iēsous legei autois hoti Ou chreian echousin hoi ischyontes iatrou allʼ hoi kakōs echontes· ouk ēlthon kalesai dikaious alla hamartōlous.

paragraphs.text: And John`s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting: and they come and say unto him, Why do John`s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but thy disciples fast not?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἦσαν οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι νηστεύοντες. καὶ ἔρχονται καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ τῶν Φαρισαίων νηστεύουσιν, οἱ δὲ σοὶ μαθηταὶ οὐ νηστεύουσιν;
paragraphs.translit: Kai ēsan hoi mathētai Iōannou kai hoi Pharisaioi nēsteuontes. kai erchontai kai legousin autō· Dia ti hoi mathētai Iōannou kai hoi mathētai tōn Pharisaiōn nēsteuousin, hoi de soi mathētai ou nēsteuousin;

paragraphs.text: And Jesus said unto them, Can the sons of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ δύνανται οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετʼ αὐτῶν ἐστιν νηστεύειν; ὅσον χρόνον ἔχουσιν τὸν νυμφίον μετʼ αὐτῶν οὐ δύνανται νηστεύειν·
paragraphs.translit: kai eipen autois ho Iēsous· Mē dynantai hoi hyioi tou nymphōnos en hō ho nymphios metʼ autōn estin nēsteuein; hoson chronon echousin ton nymphion metʼ autōn ou dynantai nēsteuein·

paragraphs.text: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then will they fast in that day.
paragraphs.original: ἐλεύσονται δὲ ἡμέραι ὅταν ἀπαρθῇ ἀπʼ αὐτῶν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ τότε νηστεύσουσιν ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ.
paragraphs.translit: eleusontai de hēmerai hotan aparthē apʼ autōn ho nymphios, kai tote nēsteusousin en ekeinē tē hēmera.

paragraphs.text: No man seweth a piece of undressed cloth on an old garment: else that which should fill it up taketh from it, the new from the old, and a worse rent is made.
paragraphs.original: Οὐδεὶς ἐπίβλημα ῥάκους ἀγνάφου ἐπιράπτει ἐπὶ ἱμάτιον παλαιόν· εἰ δὲ μή, αἴρει τὸ πλήρωμα ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ τὸ καινὸν τοῦ παλαιοῦ, καὶ χεῖρον σχίσμα γίνεται.
paragraphs.translit: Oudeis epiblēma rhakous agnaphou epiraptei epi himation palaion· ei de mē, airei to plērōma apʼ autou to kainon tou palaiou, kai cheiron schisma ginetai.

paragraphs.text: And no man putteth new wine into old wineskins; else the wine will burst the skins, and the wine perisheth, and the skins: but [they put] new wine into fresh wine-skins.
paragraphs.original: καὶ οὐδεὶς βάλλει οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς παλαιούς· εἰ δὲ μή, ῥήξει ὁ οἶνος τοὺς ἀσκούς, καὶ ὁ οἶνος ἀπόλλυται καὶ οἱ ἀσκοί. ἀλλὰ οἶνον νέον εἰς ἀσκοὺς καινούς.
paragraphs.translit: kai oudeis ballei oinon neon eis askous palaious· ei de mē, rhēxei ho oinos tous askous, kai ho oinos apollytai kai hoi askoi. alla oinon neon eis askous kainous.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass, that he was going on the sabbath day through the grainfields; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν παραπορεύεσθαι διὰ τῶν σπορίμων, καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἤρξαντο ὁδὸν ποιεῖν τίλλοντες τοὺς στάχυας.
paragraphs.translit: Kai egeneto auton en tois sabbasin paraporeuesthai dia tōn sporimōn, kai hoi mathētai autou ērxanto hodon poiein tillontes tous stachyas.

paragraphs.text: And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful?
paragraphs.original: καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ἔλεγον αὐτῷ· Ἴδε τί ποιοῦσιν τοῖς σάββασιν ὃ οὐκ ἔξεστιν;
paragraphs.translit: kai hoi Pharisaioi elegon autō· Ide ti poiousin tois sabbasin ho ouk exestin;

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, Did ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry, he, and they that were with him?
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε τί ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ὅτε χρείαν ἔσχεν καὶ ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autois· Oudepote anegnōte ti epoiēsen Dauid hote chreian eschen kai epeinasen autos kai hoi metʼ autou;

paragraphs.text: How he entered into the house of God when Abiathar was high priest, and ate the showbread, which it is not lawful to eat save for the priests, and gave also to them that were with him?
paragraphs.original: πῶς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπὶ Ἀβιαθὰρ ἀρχιερέως καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ἔφαγεν, οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ τοὺς ἱερεῖς, καὶ ἔδωκεν καὶ τοῖς σὺν αὐτῷ οὖσιν;
paragraphs.translit: pōs eisēlthen eis ton oikon tou theou epi Abiathar archiereōs kai tous artous tēs protheseōs ephagen, hous ouk exestin phagein ei mē tous hiereis, kai edōken kai tois syn autō ousin;

paragraphs.text: And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Τὸ σάββατον διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐγένετο καὶ οὐχ ὁ ἄνθρωπος διὰ τὸ σάββατον·
paragraphs.translit: kai elegen autois· To sabbaton dia ton anthrōpon egeneto kai ouch ho anthrōpos dia to sabbaton·

paragraphs.text: so that the Son of man is lord even of the sabbath.
paragraphs.original: ὥστε κύριός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ τοῦ σαββάτου.
paragraphs.translit: hōste kyrios estin ho hyios tou anthrōpou kai tou sabbatou.
